This repository contains an independent C++20 implementation of the computer
checks for Appendix B.2–B.4 of **“Three-edge coloring apex cubic graphs.”** The
implementation was reconstructed from the paper's pseudocode, the cited
free-homomorphism algorithms, the file-format specification, and the supplied
configuration and rule data. The authors' original implementation was not
consulted.

The program verifies Lemmas B.1, B.2, and B.3. It includes the dart and
pseudo-embedding data model, free homomorphisms, configuration blocking,
discharging-rule combination, cartwheel enumeration and refinement,
`allHomImages`, and an independent semi-D/semi-C reducibility checker.

## Requirements

- a C++20 compiler;
- CMake 3.20 or newer;
- Python 3 for the optional sharding and metric-checking scripts.

The code is tested with GCC and Clang. CMake also supplies appropriate warning
flags for MSVC.

## Build and test

```bash
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build -j
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
```

The verifier executable is `build/apex_verify`.

A sanitizer build can be made with:

```bash
cmake -S . -B build-asan \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS='-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer' \
  -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS='-fsanitize=address,undefined'
cmake --build build-asan -j
ctest --test-dir build-asan --output-on-failure
```

## Input data

The input data are included under `data/`:

- `data/configurations/K/` contains `K001.conf`, …, `K915.conf`;
- `data/discharging-rules/R/` contains the 70 main rule files;
- `data/discharging-rules/R_auxiliary/` contains the four auxiliary
  homomorphic-cover files.

Lemma B.3 processes configurations in lexicographic filename order. Every
command below accepts `--data-root`; its default is `data`.

The complete syntax of all input and output records is documented in
[`FORMAT.md`](FORMAT.md). In particular, an auxiliary-rule file has the form

```text
R
k
R_1
...
R_k
```

and every embedded rule record includes an explicit digon-count line, including
when that count is zero.

## Commands

Validate all bundled input files and their outer extensions:

```bash
build/apex_verify validate-data --data-root data
```

Verify Lemma B.1:

```bash
build/apex_verify b1 --data-root data
```

The optional `--combined-out DIR` argument writes the surviving combined rules.

Verify Lemma B.2:

```bash
build/apex_verify b2 --data-root data
```

The five center-degree cases can be run in separate processes:

```bash
python3 scripts/run_b2_parallel.py \
  --executable build/apex_verify \
  --data-root data \
  --jobs 2 \
  --check-metrics
```

For enumeration without the longer refinement assertion, use
`--enumeration-only` together with `--first-degree` and `--last-degree`.

Verify Lemma B.3:

```bash
build/apex_verify b3 --data-root data
```

The complete computation can be divided into filename-order shards:

```bash
python3 scripts/run_b3_parallel.py \
  --executable build/apex_verify \
  --data-root data \
  --jobs 4
```

Each shard still constructs the complete preceding configuration prefix, so its
`K_smaller` set is identical to that in the sequential computation.

Useful B.3 output and regression options are:

```text
--islands-out DIR              write generated islands
--island-occurrences FILE      write one ring count per occurrence
--skip-reducibility            enumerate without checking reducibility
--literal-search               disable the safe B.4 memoized search
--no-reducibility-cache        recompute reducibility for every occurrence
```

Run all three checks and compare their output with the reference metrics:

```bash
build/apex_verify all --data-root data | tee metrics.txt
python3 scripts/check_expected_metrics.py metrics.txt
```

## Expected metrics

| Check                                 | Expected value |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------: |
| surviving combined rules              |            747 |
| maximum combined-rule charge          |              5 |
| possible bad wheels, center degree 7  |           4438 |
| possible bad wheels, center degree 8  |           4939 |
| possible bad wheels, center degree 9  |           2409 |
| possible bad wheels, center degree 10 |            567 |
| possible bad wheels, center degree 11 |             38 |
| islands with `\|F_R(I)\| = 0`         |            254 |
| islands with `\|F_R(I)\| = 1`         |          88393 |
| islands with `\|F_R(I)\| = 2`         |          20836 |
| islands with `\|F_R(I)\| = 3`         |             18 |
| islands with `\|F_R(I)\| >= 4`        |              0 |

The B.3 values count generated occurrences. Isomorphic or repeated islands are
not removed merely because another branch produced the same isomorphism type.
The optimized search may memoize a solved state, but it replays the complete
result for every state and dart-pair occurrence. `--literal-search` is retained
as a direct regression path.

## Implementation details

`allHomImages` performs its initial configuration-blocking test without choosing
a target center vertex. The center-specific blocking routine remains separate
and is used only in the parts of the discharging and cartwheel algorithms that
actually distinguish a center.

The default B.3 implementation adds only correctness-preserving pruning:
identifications that would force a loop or incompatible degree ranges are
rejected early, and repeated isomorphic subproblems are memoized with
multiplicity-preserving replay. The semi-reducibility checker similarly caches
verdicts without suppressing occurrences.

Further implementation notes and the routine-by-routine pseudocode map are in:

- [`docs/IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md`](docs/IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md)
- [`docs/PSEUDOCODE_MAP.md`](docs/PSEUDOCODE_MAP.md)
